Hi Henrik,

I've recently ran into the following article:

"Genome-Wide Copy Number Alterations Detection in Fresh Frozen and
Matched FFPE Samples Using SNP 6.0 Arrays"
GENES, CHROMOSOMES & CANCER 47:957–964 (2008)
Marianne Tuefferd,1*† An De Bondt,2† Ilse Van DenWyngaert,2 Willem
Talloen,2 Tobias Verbeke,3
Benilton Carvalho,...

It seems it provides the definitive evidence that the GC correction is
necessary for SNP 6.0 arrays, at least in case of FFPE samples.
I am wondering if you think it would be useful to add the GC
correction to aroma.affymetrix and if yes, could you provide some
guidelines on how to implement it?
Maybe you've already done this or it's in your plan for the next version?.

Thank you,

Alex Lisovich

There is actually a GcContentNormalization class (that operates on
summarized data, i.e. ChipEffectSet:s). This implements the
(optional) GC correct step in Section 3.2.5 of the CRMA paper:

H. Bengtsson; R. Irizarry; B. Carvalho; T. Speed, Estimation and
assessment of raw copy numbers at the single locus level,
Bioinformatics, 2008. [pmid: 18204055] [doi:
10.1093/bioinformatics/btn016]

Note that in that 500K study, with that set of data and set of
preprocessing methods, we saw no effect of doing (probe) GC-content
normalization. I'm not saying it is useful to correct for, but I
should be careful saying that there "definitive evidence" that it is
needed. I say this, because I see fragment-length normalization,
GC-content normalization, curve-fit ("loess") normalization and a few
other normalization methods as correcting for *symptoms* in data, but
not necessarily the *cause*. If one can correct for the real cause,
many of these symptoms actually goes away. One such cause is
non-linearity in data and especially offset. One of the strengths
with allelic-crosstalk calibration (one implemented in CRMA) is
actually that it corrects for offset and by doing so downstream
symptoms goes away. For instance, see Fig 2 in the CRMA paper showing
that it corrects for differences in empirical distributions, i.e.
although tempting to do quantile normalization, the real cause is
simply a single offset term. Same reasoning does indeed apply to
fragment-length normalization and what I believe also GC-content
normalization.

Back to the GcContentNormalization method: Since we saw little need to
GC-content normalization, that class has been somewhat forgotten over
time and I haven't made sure that it works with the newer chip types.
It works only with 10K-500K arrays, iff one gets the correct
annotation data files from the CNAT program. I'll have to update this
to work with these newer chip types. However, in the meanwhile I
think a good proxy will be to use probe-position sequence
normalization, which is readily implemented for all Affymetrix chip
types. This will be explained in the CRMA v2 vignette, which is on my
to do list.

So, stay tuned. I'll post a message to the list when the CRMA v2
vignette is available.

/Henrik
